target.title: fix(auto-reply): defer rollover for legacy pending-reset tombstones with active runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`initSessionState` protects live transcripts from implicit rollover with `deferImplicitRolloverForActiveRun` (`src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts:689`): when a stale session still has an active reply run, the rollover is deferred so the transcript is never renamed out from under the running writer ("Implicit daily/idle rollover must not rename a transcript while that exact session's active writer is still running").

#111140 (disable automatic session resets by default) added an early return to `evaluateSessionFreshness` for the legacy `updatedAt === 0` pending-reset tombstone (`src/config/sessions/reset-policy.ts:88-91`), yielding `{ fresh: false }` **without** a `staleReason`. The deferral guard additionally requires `entryFreshness.staleReason != null` (`session.ts:694`) — a condition that was always true before #111140, when `updatedAt: 0` flowed through the daily/idle evaluation and came out stale with `staleReason: "daily"` under the old default. Post-#111140 the condition is never true for tombstoned entries, so the active-run deferral is silently skipped for exactly those sessions and the live transcript is archived mid-write.

Failure scenario: a user on a prior release has a session with the `updatedAt: 0` pending-reset marker (acknowledged shipped state — the reset-policy comment says "Older releases persisted updatedAt=0 as an explicit pending reset marker") and a reply run still active in that session. The next inbound message evaluates freshness → tombstone → `fresh: false`, no `staleReason` → deferral skipped → `<sessionId>.jsonl` is renamed to `.jsonl.reset.<ts>` while the run is still writing; the run's remaining output is split/lost across the rollover boundary. This regresses both the new `none` default and explicitly configured `daily`/`idle` policies.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `staleReason != null` condition encoded a pre-#111140 invariant (`fresh === false` ⇒ a stale reason exists) that the tombstone branch broke. Removing the condition restores the guard for every `fresh === false` entry; the tombstone carries the same live-transcript invariant the guard exists to protect. The alternative (inventing a `staleReason` for the tombstone) would mislabel the reset end reason downstream, and #111140's own test codifies the bare `{ fresh: false }` shape, so the guard site is the right place to fix.

## User Impact

Before: upgrading users with legacy pending-reset tombstones can have an active session's transcript rotated away mid-run when the next message arrives — remaining model output lands in an archived/orphaned transcript. After: tombstoned sessions with an active run defer rollover exactly like daily/idle-stale sessions; the rollover happens once the run completes.

## Evidence

- New regression test `defers rollover of a legacy pending-reset tombstone while the same session has an active run` in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` — clones the existing `defers implicit daily rollover while the same session has an active run` harness with `updatedAt: 0`. **Fails on current main** (`isNewSession === true`, transcript archived), passes with the fix.
- Full file suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` → 141/141 pass, including the pre-existing deferral tests (daily stale, queued-reservation exclusion), confirming the guard's other behaviors are unchanged.
- Sibling suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/reset-policy.test.ts` → pass (#111140's codified `{ fresh: false }` tombstone contract untouched).
- Introduced-by: #111140; pre-change behavior verified at `git show e23dde3de5^:src/config/sessions/reset-policy.ts` (no tombstone early return; `updatedAt: 0` evaluated stale with `staleReason: "daily"`).
